note: Adapted from the revision of Sands (1965), originally in English; it records the alate, the major soldier and two soldier morphs; the measurement tables are reproduced as given (alate 22 individuals from 4 localities, major soldier 92 individuals from 24 localities, minor soldier 26 individuals from 20 localities, all with range and mean); the source is an OCR of an IA scan in which the printed decimal point · was recognised as * or ', and the measurement figures were read against the context (e.g. 1·48—1·75 recorded as 1.48—1.75).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule brown to chestnut brown; vertex with 2—3 indistinct, branching yellowish brown markings, or sometimes 1 pale central spot; postclypeus, labrum, pre-ocellar region and the small postocular patches paler, yellowish brown to brown. Antennae yellow. Pronotum yellow to yellowish brown; mesonotum, metanotum, the other thoracic sclerites and the legs yellow. Abdominal tergites brown, dark sepia around the spiracles; sternites pale yellow to yellowish brown, brown around the spiracles. Wings translucent pale brown, the subcosta and radial sector yellow, the latter outlined in sepia at the base and becoming yellowish brown towards the apex; the membrane behind the radial sector with bright orange streaks; the remaining veins brown. Posterior margin of the head capsule (behind the eyes) much less than a semicircle, slightly undulate immediately behind the eyes; fontanelle Y-shaped, often slightly concave posteriorly, 2—4 times as long as broad, the lateral arms short or very short, sometimes widened at the apex; frons with 2 small branching depressions in front of the fontanelle; eyes usually oval, moderately to distinctly projecting, moderate relative to head width, eye width index 2.6—3.0; ocelli medium-sized, nearly circular to short oval, their distance from the eye 1/10—1/5 of their shortest diameter; postclypeus moderately convex, 2.2—2.6 times as broad as long, the anterior margin straight or weakly concave, the posterior margin convex, the outer corners often more rounded, the middle sometimes slightly obtuse-angled; molar plate of the right mandible with 7 ridges; antennae 15 segments (in only 1 specimen segment 3 partially subdivided), segment 3 up to 2 times as long as segment 2, segment 4 longer than segment 2 but shorter than segment 3, segments 5 and 6 about equal in length, about as long as segment 2 but thicker. The pale scent gland on the anterior margin of sternite 5 is small, 0.56—0.64 mm wide and 0.11—0.13 mm long; cerci as long as or longer than their basal width, conical or slightly nipple-shaped. Hairs on the vertex uneven in length, not forming a felt or a pad. Measurements (mm, 22 individuals, 4 localities, range/mean): head width (across the eyes) 1.48—1.75/1.57; greatest eye diameter 0.53—0.63/0.57; ocellus 0.19—0.25×0.24—0.29/0.21×0.26; ocellus to eye 0.03—0.04/0.03; pronotum width 1.33—1.68/1.48; pronotum length 0.80—1.08/0.93; hind tibia length 1.98—2.38/2.21; fore-wing length 14.10—20.30/17.07.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Major soldier: head capsule orange yellow to rusty orange, usually orange; nasus rusty orange to chestnut brown with a red tip, usually rusty; pronotum, mesonotum and metanotum orange yellow; antennae and legs yellow; abdominal tergites yellowish brown to brown, sternites pale yellow. Head capsule in dorsal view slightly to distinctly humped behind the antennae, rounded posteriorly, as long as or slightly longer than broad, the middle of the posterior margin often slightly concave; nasus weakly conical, usually with a progressively stronger arcuate constriction from the nearly cylindrical apex towards the base (like an inverted trumpet). In lateral view from nearly straight to distinctly concave, the occiput rising and rounded behind the antennal sockets. Nasus as long as or shorter than the rest of the head capsule, usually gradually thickening from the nearly cylindrical apex to the distinctly conical base. Fontanelle large, 0.05—0.10 mm in diameter. Antennae 12—14 segments, 87% with 13, the proportions of the basal segments variable, usually segment 3 up to 2 times as long as segment 2, segments 4, 5 and 6 longer than segments 2 and 3 and shorter than segment 3. Conspicuous head setae confined to the densely hairy tip of the nasus, the dorsal surface of the head capsule with only very sparse microscopic short hairs. Median abdominal tergites almost hairless, the last two with short, sparse hairs; sternites with short, sparse, backward-directed setae about 1/6—1/3 as long as the hairs on their posterior margin, arranged roughly in longitudinal rows, 2 or 3 on each side of the midline, directed downwards or slightly forwards. Minor soldier: colour as in the major soldier, but the nasus usually chestnut brown; antennae 12 segments. Measurements (mm): major soldier (92 individuals, 24 localities) head length to the tip of the nasus 1.90—2.50/2.21; head width 1.05—1.54/1.26; head capsule depth 0.78—1.07/0.92; pronotum width 0.50—0.68/0.58; pronotum length 0.23—0.29/0.25; hind tibia length 1.20—1.55/1.37. Minor soldier (26 individuals, 20 localities) head length to the tip of the nasus 1.35—1.79/1.51; head width 0.55—0.80/0.64; head capsule depth 0.45—0.64/0.52; pronotum width 0.35—0.47/0.41; pronotum length 0.15—0.22/0.19; hind tibia length 1.08—1.33/1.19.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate can in most cases be distinguished from sympatric close relatives by the 15-segmented antennae (in the few togoensis that also have 15 segments, segment 3 is usually partially subdivided on at least one side and other characters differ). The soldier varies greatly in lateral view, the straightness and shape of the nasus (nearly conical, inverted trumpet-shaped or nearly cylindrical) depending on where the arcuate constriction begins; the base of the nasus occasionally has a slight swelling; the reduced soldier mandibles occasionally bear a small tooth. Specimens from higher elevations (up to 5000 feet) are larger. This paper sinks T. anriterrae Sjöstedt, T. maxidanicus Sjöstedt, Nasutitermes bettonianus sulciceps Emerson and N. lutzi Emerson as new synonyms of this species.
